subject: SLA definitions for inference failover windows and crediting
messages:
From: Jules Martin <jules@acme-robotics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-robotics.com
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA definitions for inference failover windows and crediting

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked promising. Procurement asked me to get written clarity on how you would treat regional failovers for our inference workloads. Specifically:

- When a region-level failover happens (traffic routed from us-west to us-east), how do you measure "uptime" for service credit eligibility? Do you calculate on per-region egress or a global control-plane health?
- If a model variant fallback (e.g., quantized vs FP16) is used automatically during capacity pressures, does that count as a service degradation eligible for credits?
- What maintenance windows are excluded from crediting, and how far in advance will customers be notified for planned maintenance affecting inference endpoints?

Attached is our procurement team's preferred template (Acme_SLA_request_v2.pdf) with some redline comments. Can you review and propose specific language we can put in the MSA/Order Form? Ideally we'd like a short mutual action plan and a 1-week turnaround on redlines.

Best,
Jules
Procurement Manager
Acme Robotics

Attachments: Acme_SLA_request_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SLA definitions for inference failover windows and crediting

Jules — thanks for the detailed note and the template. Looping in Laura for legal redline guidance and Aditya on runtime behavior. High-level responses below; I'll follow up with a proposed markup.

Quick answers:
1) Uptime measurement: we recommend scoping uptime for billing/credits to the customer-visible inference endpoint (per-endpoint token-generation success rate and latency). For multi-region customers we can expose per-region metrics; credits will be calculated per-region based on successful request rate to the endpoint in that region over the measurement window (not control-plane-only).

2) Model variant fallback: we treat automatic, pre-configured fallbacks (e.g., quantized variant with identical API contract) as a functional mitigation, not an outage, unless the fallback causes incorrect or clearly degraded responses. We can add language that credits apply when the inference endpoint returns 5xx errors, or sustained latency above an agreed threshold for N minutes (example: P1 — latency > 2s for > 10 minutes).

3) Maintenance windows: standard planned maintenance (announced 72+ hours in advance) is excluded from credits. Emergency maintenance and forced capacity migrations will be evaluated — where migration causes request failures, credits apply per the order form.

I'll attach a short proposed redline (k_iyer_proposed_sla_markup.docx) that (a) defines "Endpoint Uptime" vs "Control Plane Availability", (b) provides a step function for credits tied to sustained error-rate and latency thresholds, and (c) caps monthly credits to X% of monthly spend (we'll propose 50% cap as starting point).

Proposed next steps (can we do a 30-min call next Tue?):
- Karthik to share proposed markup (today)
- Laura to provide legal comments (T+2 days)
- Jules to confirm Acme's redline priorities (T+3 days)

—Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLA definitions for inference failover windows and crediting

Hi all,

Thanks for the draft, Karthik. A few legal points to flag before we finalize language for the MSA/Order Form:

1) Definition precision — "Endpoint Uptime" must include the exact metric and the measurement source (we prefer: successful 2xx responses as recorded in the customer-specific telemetry stream we expose via the Console API). Avoid vague terms like "successful request" without the status code definition.

2) Credits cap — we generally accept a monthly cap on credits but prefer a sliding cap tied to committed spend tiers. Example wording: "Monthly credits shall not exceed the lesser of (i) 50% of monthly fees for the affected service, or (ii) committed monthly baseline spend for the relevant Order Form."

3) Failover attribution — propose we add a clause requiring Redwood to provide a post-incident report for any region failover within 72 hours that includes root cause, mitigation taken, and a traffic map showing inbound request distribution. This is necessary for Acme to validate credit eligibility.

4) Maintenance notice windows — 72 hours for standard maintenance is fine; for rolling infra upgrades that may impact sustained latency, we should include an "advance advisory" (7 calendar days) for planned model or runtime upgrades that could change behavior.

5) Emergency maintenance carveout — we should limit "emergency maintenance" carveouts to situations where continuing service would cause data loss or significant platform risk (so customers aren't deprived of credits for predictable capacity migrations).

I will return redlines to the Word doc and add suggested legal phrasing for the post-incident report requirement. Happy to review together on Tue.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik and Laura — this is helpful. A couple clarifying Qs from procurement:

- For the latency threshold example (P1 > 2s for > 10 minutes) can you confirm whether that is measured at the 95th or 99th percentile? We usually ask for 99th p95 is ambiguous.
- For fallback variants: we want to avoid cases where the fallback is significantly lower quality (e.g., hallucination rate increases) but still returns 2xx. Can you add an explicit exclusion: credits apply when automated fallback results in measurable correctness regressions for our eval tests (we can provide a small eval set)?

If you can add those items to the markup, procurement will triage and get back with prioritized redlines. Also, we prefer DocuSign for the signature step — I included a placeholder in the doc.

Jules — thanks, noted. Quick update and mutual action plan below.

Summary of agreed items to include in redline:
- Measurement: 99th percentile (p99) latency and error-rate (5xx) measured per-endpoint per-region as reported by Redwood Console telemetry. Successful requests defined as HTTP 2xx.
- Crediting triggers: sustained p99 latency above agreed thresholds (P1: >2s for >=10 continuous minutes) OR 5xx error rate > 1% sustained for >=5 continuous minutes.
- Model fallback clause: automated fallbacks that maintain API contract will not automatically exclude credits. However, credits apply if a measurable correctness regression on an agreed eval set is observed within the incident window. Acme to provide a 200-sample eval set for test criteria; Redwood will run and share the comparison in the post-incident report.
- Maintenance: standard planned maintenance (announced 72+ hours) excluded. Notifications for major runtime or model upgrades that may affect behavior: 7 calendar days advisory.
- Credits cap: month cap = min(50% of affected service fees, committed monthly baseline).
- Post-incident report: Redwood will provide report within 72 hours for any regional failover (including traffic maps and root cause analysis).

Action items & timeline:
1) Karthik to incorporate the above points into the Word markup and return today (done — attached).
2) Laura to add clean legal phrasing around "post-incident report" and "emergency maintenance" by Thu EOD.
3) Jules / Acme to send the eval sample set and confirm whether the DocuSign flow is acceptable by Fri.
4) Optional call: Thu 9am PT to walk legal redlines if needed.

If that all looks right I can start a tracked-change markup and we can move the order form to signature after legal alignment.

Thanks — Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
